messages.subject: melting arrays
parts:
I have an array constructed by daply and want to plot parts of it with ggplot2. Under the impression that ggplot works well with melted data, I melted the array,
b <- melt(big)
g <- ggplot(data=b, aes(KB, reclen))
g+geom_point(aes(colour=random_read), size=2) + facet_grid(plus ~ minus)
yielding
Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'random_read' not found

How can I get this to work?

> dim(big)
[1] 5 5 126 8
> names(dimnames(big))
[1] "plus" "minus" "" ""

The documentation on melting arrays is extremely terse (the journal article refers to the online docs; ?melt.array's *entire* Details section is "This code is conceptually similar to 'as.data.frame.table'". ?as.data.frame.table yields nothing.

The first 2 dimensions have all combinations of the integers 1 to 5. The last dimension has 8 columns, the first 2 of which are case identifiers (KB and reclen) and the others represent values of interest.
> dimnames(big)[[4]]
[1] "KB" "reclen" "write" "rewrite" "read"
[6] "reread" "random_read" "random_write"


The contents of b look odd to me:
> head(b)
plus minus Var.3 Var.4 value
1 1 1 v KB 6
2 2 1 v KB 6
3 3 1 v KB 6
4 4 1 v KB 6
5 5 1 v KB 6
6 1 2 v KB 7

> tail(b)
plus minus Var.3 Var.4 value
25195 5 4 v random_write 0
25196 1 5 v random_write 0
25197 2 5 v random_write 0
25198 3 5 v random_write 0
25199 4 5 v random_write 0
25200 5 5 v random_write 0

Somewhere along the way I picked up row labels that were all v, which obviously isn't too helpful.

parts:
Well, the melted object is a data.frame, though not setup appropriately. As detailed below, I've been unable to cast to a properly setup data.frame even though I seem to have the d*ply under better control.

I would still like to know how to melt an array, but I switched to ddply instead of dapply, I ran into an odd problem with the melt, and a show-stopper while trying to cast to a data.frame appropriate for ggplot.

> big <- ddply(small,.(plus, minus), function(coords) {
+ plusi <- c(coords$plus)
+ minusi <- c(coords$minus)
+ plus <- ms[[plusi]]$mean
+ delta <- plus[,3:8] - ms[[minusi ]]$mean[,3:8]
+ cbind(test, delta)
+ })
> dim(big)
[1] 3150 10
> colnames(big)
[1] "plus" "minus" "KB" "reclen" "write"
[6] "rewrite" "read" "reread" "random_read" "random_write"
> b <- melt(big, measured=colnames(big)[4:10])
Using as id variables

The odd problem is the blank list of id variables; I thought it was supposed to default to everything else.

The result was short of information:
> dim(b)
[1] 31500 2
> colnames(b)
[1] "variable" "value"

I think I worked around that problem by being explicit:
> b <- melt(big, measured=colnames(big)[5:10], id=colnames(big)[1:4])
> dim(b)
[1] 18900 6
> colnames(b)
[1] "plus" "minus" "KB" "reclen" "variable" "value"

But then comes the show-stopper:
> head(b)
plus minus KB reclen variable value
1 1 1 6 2 write 0
2 1 1 6 3 write 0
3 1 1 6 4 write 0
4 1 1 6 5 write 0
5 1 1 6 6 write 0
6 1 1 7 2 write 0
> bc <- cast(b, random_read ~ plus + minus + KB + reclen)
Error: Casting formula contains variables not found in molten data: random_read
> unique(b$variable)
[1] write rewrite read reread random_read
[6] random_write
Levels: write rewrite read reread random_read random_write

So even though the variable seems to be present, cast can't find it. I also tried using read to see if the _ was causing trouble; read didn't work either.

Perhaps some earlier problems with reshape2 are relevant. It seems unlikely since most indications are I don't have the package; however note there is one reference to a prior installation:
> install.packages("reshape2")
trying URL 'http://cran.cnr.berkeley.edu/bin/windows/contrib/3.1/reshape2_1.4.zip'
Content type 'application/zip' length 498287 bytes (486 Kb)
opened URL
downloaded 486 Kb

The downloaded binary packages are in
C:\Users\rdboylan\AppData\Local\Temp\Rtmpm2yGjE\downloaded_packages
> library(help="reshape2")
Error in find.package(pkgName, lib.loc, verbose = verbose) :
there is no package called 'reshape2'
In addition: Warning message:
In read.dcf(file.path(p, "DESCRIPTION"), c("Package", "Version")) :
cannot open compressed file 'c:/Program Files/R/R-3.1.2/library/reshape2/DESCRIPTION', probable reason 'No such file or directory'

Ross

column for each of the original dimensions, and a column containing

> Using as id variables
>

These examples are not very useful to your potential helper, because
we cannot reproduce theme. Please make as simple self-contained
example that we can run and correct, that way we can actually help you
find a solution rather than guessing as to what you are trying to do.

However, in this case I can spot at least one error, which is that you
have incorrectly named the "measure.vars" argument. If you look at the
documentation for melt.data.frame, you will find that there is no
argument named "measured".

have to exist in the data.frame.

x <- cast(dd, ID ~ variable)
